passage: "Dilnaz, got a minute? Just us." "If it's about the rent, I'll pay Monday." "It's not the rent. You've skipped dinner all week. You cancelled the film, and the birthday." "I'm busy, Sharmila." "And yesterday you said, 'What's the point of any of it.' I keep thinking about that." "It was a joke. Don't lecture me." "I won't. I'm not here to fix anything. I just miss you, and I'm worried." A long silence. Dilnaz picks at her sleeve. "Everything's just... heavy. All the time." "Okay. Thank you for telling me. I'm staying right here." "I don't know what to do." "Would you see the campus counsellor? I can book it with you, right now. I'll walk you there." "...Only if you come." "I'm coming."

qa.q: What did Dilnaz cancel, according to Sharmila?
qa.a: The film, and the birthday.

qa.q: How does Sharmila feel about the changes she has noticed in Dilnaz?
qa.a: She feels worried and misses Dilnaz, saying so plainly, and keeps thinking about the remark 'What's the point of any of it.'

qa.q: Which of Sharmila's choices helped Dilnaz open up?
qa.a: Sharmila checked in privately, named what was noticed, promised not to lecture, and simply stayed.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz see Sharmila's offer to walk with her?
qa.a: She may feel less alone and more able to go, since she agrees only if Sharmila comes.

grounding: Sharmila notices missed meals, cancelled plans and dark remarks, checks in privately, listens and stays present, and gently encourages professional help.

passage: I'm Tenzin. Last year my roommate Jagdish slowly disappeared in front of me, and I almost didn't notice. First it was meals. He'd say he'd eaten, but his plate stayed clean in the rack. Then he pulled out of the trek we'd planned for months. Then the remarks: "Nothing I do matters anyway." I laughed the first time. I'm not proud of that. The third time, I shut the door and sat on his bed. "You don't have to talk. But I've noticed you're not eating, and I'm worried about you." He didn't say anything for a long time. Then he said, "I'm so tired of feeling like this." I didn't try to fix it. I just stayed. Over the next week I kept asking gently, and in the end he let me go with him to the college doctor.

qa.q: What trip did Jagdish pull out of?
qa.a: The trek they had planned for months.

qa.q: How did Tenzin feel by the third remark, and what shows it?
qa.a: Tenzin was worried about Jagdish; Tenzin shut the door, sat on his bed and said, 'I'm worried about you.'

qa.q: What did Tenzin do after the third remark that helped?
qa.a: Tenzin shut the door, spoke privately, named the worry, stayed without trying to fix it, and later went with him to the doctor.

qa.q: How might Jagdish have felt when Tenzin laughed at the first remark?
qa.a: He may have felt unheard and more alone, which could have made it harder to speak up.

grounding: A roommate recalls noticing missed meals, cancelled plans and dark remarks, checking in privately, staying present and encouraging professional help.

passage:
Hostel floor note, Wednesday night. Written by Lavanya, senior floor monitor.
Over the last two weeks I've seen Gurpreet skip dinner at the mess at least five times. She cancelled our Sunday movie plan twice. Today at the laundry she said, "What's even the point of me being here?" and laughed, but it wasn't a joke laugh.
I went to her room at nine, just the two of us. I asked her straight how she was really doing. She cried and said she'd been feeling empty for weeks. I asked if she was thinking of hurting herself; she said no, but she was scared by how dark her thoughts felt. I stayed with her, and with her agreement we told the warden together that same night. Tomorrow at ten, I'm walking her to the counselling centre.

qa.q: How many times did Gurpreet skip dinner at the mess?
qa.a: She skipped dinner at least five times over two weeks.

qa.q: How did Lavanya feel hearing Gurpreet's remark at the laundry?
qa.a: Lavanya felt worried and alarmed, sensing the laugh wasn't a joke, and decided to check in that same evening.

qa.q: What did Lavanya do that showed real care?
qa.a: Lavanya checked in privately, asked directly, listened, stayed, told the warden with Gurpreet that night and arranged to walk her to the counselling centre.

qa.q: How might Gurpreet feel when Lavanya came to her room?
qa.a: She may have felt relieved and less alone to have someone notice and ask how she was really doing.

grounding: Shows a friend noticing missed meals, cancelled plans and dark remarks, checking in privately, staying present and encouraging professional help.

passage:
Friday night, very late
Hemant has skipped the mess for days. He cancelled cricket three Saturdays in a row. And in the library today he said, "Wouldn't matter if I just disappeared."
So after dinner I went to his room. I just sat on the floor and said, "Hey. I'm worried about you. How are you actually?" He was quiet for ages. Then he said he's been feeling empty since the exams and sometimes wishes he wouldn't wake up.
I didn't leave. I said, "I'm really glad you told me." We called the campus helpline together, right there. Then, with his okay, we went down to the warden, who called his parents. His dad is driving here tonight.
Tomorrow I'm going with him to the counsellor.
Pooja

qa.q: How many Saturdays did Hemant cancel cricket?
qa.a: He cancelled cricket three Saturdays in a row.

qa.q: How was Pooja feeling in the library when Hemant made his remark?
qa.a: Pooja felt worried and alarmed enough to go to his room that same evening.

qa.q: Which of Pooja's actions kept Hemant safe that night?
qa.a: Pooja stayed with him, called the campus helpline with him and went with him to the warden, who called his parents the same night.

qa.q: How might Hemant have felt when Pooja said she was glad he told her?
qa.a: He may have felt relieved and less ashamed, knowing his friend would not judge or leave him.

grounding: Shows a friend noticing missed meals, cancelled plans and dark remarks, checking in privately, staying present and getting help that same night.

passage:
Alka had been annoyed with Tarun for weeks. He had cancelled their Sunday walk to the temple tank twice, skipped her sister's engagement, and stopped answering in the group chat. In the college canteen in Sangli, he pushed his plate away again.
When she joked, "Coming to the fair on Friday?" he muttered, "What's the point. Nothing's going to get better anyway."
The words stayed with her. That evening she went to his house and asked him to sit with her on the steps, away from the others. "You haven't been eating, and what you said today scared me. Are you thinking of hurting yourself?"
He looked at his hands. "No. I'm just so tired of everything."
Alka stayed. She listened for a long time. Before she left, with his okay, they told his elder sister together, and his sister booked the college counsellor for the next morning. Alka texted him before bed: "I'm here."

qa.q: What did Tarun mutter when Alka asked about the fair?
qa.a: "What's the point. Nothing's going to get better anyway."

qa.q: How did Alka's feelings change after Tarun's remark?
qa.a: Her annoyance at the cancelled plans turned into worry and fear for him; the words stayed with her.

qa.q: What did Alka do that showed real care?
qa.a: She checked in privately that same evening, asked directly, listened and stayed, involved his sister and encouraged the counsellor visit, then texted before bed.

qa.q: How might Tarun feel when Alka turns up at his house?
qa.a: He might feel exposed at first, then less alone and cared for because she came to him rather than giving up.

grounding: Alka notices Tarun's missed meals, cancelled plans and dark remark, checks in privately, listens and stays, and gently gets him professional help.
